title: Lesson 21 - Freshness, Refresh Cadence and Retrieval Failure Modes
description: Explain the considerations of Agentforce Data Library and its concepts.

questions.question: An agent keeps citing a procedure you retired last week, and the library reports healthy. What is the most likely cause?
options: The agent is missing the Service Planner.
The search index was not refreshed after the source changed, so it still holds the old chunk.
The running user lacks the Allow View Knowledge permission.
The org has run out of Data 360 credits.
questions.explanation: The retriever returns whatever chunk is in the index, and that chunk is stale until the stream refreshes and the index rebuilds.

questions.question: A search index for a new library never reaches ready. Where do you look first?
options: The data stream, data lake and data model objects, and their mapping, which must be successful and active before the index is created.
The running user's data space name.
questions.explanation: The search index is created only after the stream, objects and mapping are all successful and active, so a stalled index is an upstream Data 360 problem.

questions.question: Which statement about re-indexing cost is correct?
options: Data libraries consume Data 360 credits, and re-indexing that re-chunks content spends more.
Re-indexing is always free and instant regardless of corpus size.
Only the LLM call consumes credits, not indexing.
Data 360 credits apply only to web search libraries.
questions.explanation: Data libraries consume Data 360 credits and each refresh that re-chunks content spends more, so re-indexing is a budgeted operation and unused indexes should be deleted.
